zh.title: United與American迫使O'Hare（ORD）加速建設24個登機門候機廳
zh.summary: 因兩家航空公司快速增長，O'Hare加速建設24個登機門E候機廳
body: 根據媒體 Simple Flying 於2026年8月21日的報導，由於 United 與 American 的快速增長正將 O'Hare 機場推向容量上限，該機場目前正在加速建設擁有24個登機門的 E 候機廳（Concourse E），以應對緊繃的機場運能。
報導指出，這兩家航空公司的快速擴張導致 O'Hare 機場正面臨登機門不足的限制。為了緩解日益嚴重的容量壓力，機場決定加快推進這座擁有24個登機門的 E 候機廳項目，解決因航空公司增長而帶來的空間挑戰。

en.title: United and American Growth Forces O'Hare (ORD) to Accelerate 24-Gate Concourse
en.summary: O'Hare is accelerating its Concourse E project as United and American rapid growth nears airport capacity.
body: According to a report published by Simple Flying on August 21, 2026, O’Hare is currently accelerating the construction of its 24-gate Concourse E. This acceleration comes as the rapid growth of United and American continues to push the major airport closer toward its operational capacity.

The airport is running out of gates due to this rapid expansion, forcing O’Hare to speed up the Concourse E development. The acceleration of the 24-gate concourse project is a direct response to the growth of United and American, which has pushed the airport to find solutions to address its capacity limits.

zh.title: 英國國防部公布軍機統計 旋翼機隊減少27架定翼機升至507架
zh.summary: 英國國防部；軍用旋翼機總數降至249架；定翼機隊增至507架；無人機系統達189架
body: 英國國防部於2026年8月20日發布年度軍用航空器統計資料。根據這項截至2026年4月1日的最新數據，英國軍方的旋翼機（直升機）總數降至249架，相較於一年前的統計數據減少了27架。根據外媒 AeroTime 報導，國防部數據顯示軍方整體航空器編制出現顯著結構調整。
英國國防部指出，旋翼機數量減少的主要原因，在於皇家空軍退役了服役長達54年的美洲豹（Puma）直升機，該機型已於2025年3月正式走入歷史。國防部先前曾於2024年11月宣布相關裁減計畫，預計退役17架 Puma 直升機與14架契努克（Chinook）直升機以節省運作成本。目前 Chinook 仍是英國軍方規模最大的旋翼機隊，現役數量為45架。

與旋翼機的減少趨勢相反，英國軍方的定翼機總數量有所增加，自上一年度增加3架至507架。國防部將定翼機數量的增長歸因於持續接收洛克希德·馬丁（Lockheed Martin）公司生產的 F-35 閃電II（F-35 Lightning II）戰鬥機。與此同時，颱風（Typhoon）戰鬥機仍是英國最大規模的定翼機隊，現有數量為124架，不過該機隊數量正持續減少，皇家空軍已於2025年4月1日退役絕大部分的第一批次（Tranche 1）颱風戰機。
在無人機系統方面，符合國防部認證或S2類別規範的無人駕駛航空器系統數量增加9架，達到189架。國防部統計資料補充說明，掠奪者（Reaper）無人機已於2025年10月正式退役，並由守護者（Protector）無人機系統接替其任務。此項統計並不包含未達到認證門檻的較小型無人機系統。
在機隊可用率方面，統計顯示定翼機與旋翼機的妥善管理率均有所提升。在納入主動機隊管理紀錄的374架定翼機中，有323架（即86%）被列為現役妥善狀態，高於前一年的82%。而在213架記錄的旋翼機平台中，有165架（即77%）處於現役妥善狀態，亦高於2025年記錄的70%。國防部說明，主動管理定義包含處於封存狀態的飛機，而由合約承包營運的航空器則未納入可用率的分母計算。

en.title: UK MoD Fleet Data Shows Rotary Wing Inventory Down to 249 as Fixed Wing Rises
en.summary: UK Ministry of Defence reports military helicopter fleet fell to 249 while fixed-wing inventory rose to 507.
body: The UK Ministry of Defence released its annual military aircraft inventory statistics on August 20, 2026. According to the official data snapshot reflecting the status as of April 1, 2026, the total UK military rotary-wing inventory fell to 249 platforms, representing a decline of 27 aircraft compared to the same period one year earlier. Industry outlet AeroTime reported that the official release outlines substantial structural shifts across the armed forces.

The Ministry of Defence attributed the decline in rotary-wing platforms primarily to the disposal of Puma helicopters, which the Royal Air Force officially withdrew from active service in March 2025 after 54 years of operations. The MoD had previously announced in November 2024 a cost-saving measures package that included retiring 17 Pumas and 14 Chinooks. Despite the reduction, the Chinook remains the largest single rotary-wing fleet type in the inventory, with 45 aircraft recorded.

In contrast to the decline in helicopters, the UK fixed-wing military aircraft inventory moved in the opposite direction, increasing by three platforms to reach a total of 507. The MoD attributed this increase directly to the ongoing onboarding of Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II stealth fighters. Meanwhile, the Typhoon remains the largest fixed-wing fleet in service at 124 aircraft, though its numbers continue to decrease following the Royal Air Force retiring the majority of its Tranche 1 Typhoons as of April 1, 2025.

During the same reporting period, uncrewed aircraft systems operating under the MoD's certified or S2 regulatory categories increased by nine platforms to a total of 189. The official statistics noted that the Reaper system went out of service in October 2025 and has been successfully replaced by the Protector platform. Smaller uncrewed systems that do not meet the specified regulatory certification thresholds fall outside of this official tally.

Operational availability metrics showed improvements across both rotary-wing and fixed-wing fleets. Among the 374 tracked fixed-wing aircraft subject to active fleet management, 323 aircraft (or 86%) were counted as in service, up from 82% recorded in the previous year. For rotary-wing aircraft, 165 out of 213 platforms (or 77%) were in service as of April 1, 2026, compared with 70% in 2025. The MoD defines in-service status as any airframe under active management, including stored platforms, while contracted platforms are excluded from availability calculations.
